key_insight: Integrating uncertainty estimates with nnU-Net enables budget-aware prioritization of manual QA so clinicians inspect the regions most likely to contain segmentation errors, improving safety and efficiency for radiotherapy planning.
problem_solved: Reduces the time-consuming, high-risk task of manually checking Clinical Target Volume (CTV) delineations—especially for complex treatments like TMLI—by providing reliable cues about where automated segmentations may be wrong and allocating limited reviewer time effectively.
method: Produce nnU-Net segmentations plus per-voxel uncertainty maps (e.g., test-time augmentation/ensembling or probabilistic outputs).
Aggregate uncertainty into region/case-level scores and rank segmentations or subregions by expected error under a reviewer time/budget constraint.
Present prioritized overlays and suggested review targets to clinicians in a human-in-the-loop QA loop to maximize error detection given limited review resources.
impact: Enables practical, risk-aware deployment of auto-segmentation in radiotherapy by focusing manual effort where it matters most, lowering review burden while preserving or improving clinical safety. Useful blueprint for ML teams building QA pipelines in safety-critical imaging applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: nnU-Net → uncertainty map → budget-aware ranking → clinician review loop.
CT slice with segmentation and overlaid uncertainty heatmap (high uncertainty highlighted).
Bar/stacked-chart showing reviewer time budget vs. cumulative detected errors when using budget-aware ranking vs. random/naive review.
Schematic of prioritized region list or case queue presented to clinician (human-in-the-loop icon).
paper_title: Budget-Aware Uncertainty for Radiotherapy Segmentation QA Using nnU-Net
paper_authors: Ricardo Coimbra Brioso, Lorenzo Mondo, Damiano Dei, Nicola Lambri, Pietro Mancosu
